We use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(14{cos}^{2}⁡x-5{x}^{2}+14{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(14({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)-5{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(14\cdot 1-5{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(14-5{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =(14x-\frac{5}{3}{x}^{3})\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =[14\pi -\frac{5}{3}{\pi }^{3}]-[14\cdot 0-\frac{5}{3}\cdot {0}^{3}] \\  & =14\pi -\frac{5{\pi }^{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
